newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - Foodcorp yr share seen up 13 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Foodcorp yr share seen up 13 pct.

text.p: South African diversified food group Foodcorp Ltd is expected to post a modest improvement in year profits amid mixed performances from its divisions and joint venture operations.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast fully diluted attributable year earnings rising about 13.6 percent to between 262 and 267 cents per share with a consensus of 264.7 cents.
Forecasts on a dividend ranged from 80 to 121 cents.

The wide dividend range reflects the difficulty of predicting a pay-out as Foodcorp did not post a dividend at the 1995 yearend in anticipation of the abolition of Secondary Tax on Companies, analysts said.
Analysts said Foodcorp's earnings would be hemmed in by a diluted contribution from snacks operation Simba following the sale last year of a 50 percent stake to PepsiCo Foods International.
"They will be sorry to have lost 50 percent of the Simba earnings to PepsiCo. Last year earnings were only partially diluted," said a food analyst who asked not to be identified.
But another analyst said that although the sale to PepsiCo would reduce Foodcorp operating profit, it would be recovered on the interest line as Foodcorp held cash from the sale.
Pillsbury Brands Africa, a joint venture with the U.S. Pillsbury Company, is expected to have had another bad year, analysts said. "It has been slow to take off," an analyst said.
A solid performance was seen from the group's fishing operation, Marine Products.
"The fishing operations have had a pretty good year," said an analyst, adding that the pilchard catch had been solid although anchovies had disappointed.
Strong contributions are also expected from the Enterprise Foods division, a joint venture with ICS Holdings Ltd and Nola's grain-based operations.
Analysts said all eyes would in 1997 be on the unbundling of Foodcorp from parent Malbak Ltd, which in August gave the go-ahead for the unbundling of its assets.
At the time Malbak, which owns a 66 percent stake in Foodcorp, said any asset distribution would be made during the first quarter of the 1997 calender year.
